name: Bin Xu
title: Assistant Professor
researchAreas: Reinforcement learning for vehicle energy management
fitReason: Established Assistant Professor with an explicit unfunded graduate/visiting-scholar inquiry route and current supervised neural vehicle-control hardware. The 2021 OU arrival is secondary to the recent-AP preference. Physical evidence is actuator-level validation, with important limits stated in the full paper.

physicalEvidence.summary: The complete July 2026 Sensors paper tests a real 2025 Nissan Leaf in OU’s lab, held stationary on rotating supports. A trained MLP forward model supplies synthetic examples for a learned inverse steering map, used as feedforward with integral feedback. Section 4.2 runs that neural controller in closed loop through the vehicle electronics, reaching ±135° commands; negative-direction overshoot and CAN-feedback glitches remain. The separately tested PID covers a wider range, so its performance is not attributed to the neural controller. Moving-vehicle path tracking remains future work in this paper. Xu is explicitly the supervisor, resource provider and project administrator; the current lab roster identifies the first author as his doctoral student. The official 2026 fleet article verifies wider current vehicle testing but does not prove that this neural controller performed autonomous road navigation.

shortVisit.summary: The live openings page separates PhD intake from a broader invitation to visiting scholars and graduate/undergraduate students interested in research. The latter explicitly has no funding. This supports a genuine research inquiry, but outside-master acceptance, proposed project, summer 2027, duration and campus presence still require agreement. The university separately has an applicable outside-master Student Intern route; that policy is not a PI offer.
